==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|defæcate|qq1=archaic|defaecate}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:bor|la:dēfaecātus|tree=1}}
{{bor+|en|la|dēfaecātus}}, the {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|dēfaecō}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} and {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}. See also {{m|en|faeces}}; cognate with {{cog|fr|déféquer}}.

===Pronunciation===
{{q|verb}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈdɛfɪkeɪt/}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-defecate.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-defecate1.wav|a=Southern England}}
{{q|adjective}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈdɛfɪkət/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-defecate2.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[excrete]] [[feces]] from one's [[bowels]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}}
## To [[pass#Verb|pass]] (something) as [[excrement]]; to [[purge#Verb|purge]].
## {{lb|en|also|figurative}} To [[clean#Verb|clean]] (something) of [[dregs]], [[impurity|impurities]], etc.; to [[purify]].
##* {{RQ:Glanvill Vanity of Dogmatizing|chapter=III|page=22|passage=[I]f vve '''defæcate''' the notion from materiality, {{...}} it vvill be as hard to apprehend, as that an empty vviſh ſhould remove Mountains: a ſuppoſition vvhich if realized, vvould relieve ''[[w:Sisyphus|Siſyphus]]''.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|passage={{...}} I ſhall add, that proſecuting a hint a happened to meet with in the diſcourſe of a wandering chymiſt, I practiſed a way ſo to '''defecate''' the dark and muddy oil of amber drawn ''per ſe'', that a pretty proportion of it would come over ſo tranſparent and finely coloured, that the experiment did not a little pleaſe thoſe I ſhewed it to.|year=1744|author=w:Robert Boyle|deriv=compilation|original=Certain phyſiological eſsays and other tracts written at diſtant times, and on ſeveral occaſions by the honourable Robert Boyle ; wherein ſome of the tracts are enlarged by experiments and the work is increaſed by the addition of a diſcourse about the abſolute reſt in bodies.|url=http://name.umdl.umich.edu/A28944.0001.001|by=w:Robert Boyle|coauthors=Thomas Birch|editor=w:Thomas Birch|title=The Works of the Honourable Robert Boyle: In Five Volumes : to which is Prefixed, the Life of the Author|volume=1|section=part VI: Certain Physiological Essays, and other tracts written at diſtant Times, eſsay 7: The Hiſtory of Fluidity and Firmneſs, the ſecond part: of Firmneſs|pageurl=https://books.google.com.sg/books?id=_-J2h0qXP30C&pg=265|page=265}}
##* {{RQ:Burton Melancholy|edition=2nd|5=224|passage=Some are of opinion that such fat, standing waters make the best beer, and that seething doth '''defecate''' it {{...}}}}
